newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa shares seen up next week on pent-up demand.
newsitem.headline: South Africa shares seen up next week on pent-up demand.

text.p: South African shares could firm next week if problems with the exchange's electronic trading system are fixed enabling it to meet pent-up demand.
Portfolio managers and dealers said the approach of the December futures expiry and the fourth quarter unit trust close-out would also prop up shares.
They said a lot of investors were nervous to play the market this week due to the erratic trade caused by response problems with the Johannesburg Equities Trading (Jet) system.
"If the system works next week, at some stage we should see a turnaround (to firmness)," said Raymond Goss, a portfolio manager at Irish & Co.
"Maybe December will be the start of the turn, getting in line with world markets," he said.

The Johannesburg Stock Exchange lost almost 11 hours of trading this week after new software installed at the weekend began to play up. The bourse decided on Wednesday to revert to its original system and re-evaluate the new software.
Dealers said investment managers, in a bid to show a strong performance on their portfolios, may try to push the market up ahead of the end of the unit trust quarter.
"In order for unit trusts to perform you need to push the market up by about 300 points. They can still kick it (market) up on unit trusts and futures close-out," a dealer said.
Rhett Hammond, portfolio manager at Investec Asset Management said another positive for the market next week was that it was starting to look cheap for investors.
Goss said insurance and banking stocks may still offer some value.
A stronger rand this week could also invite investors back to the market next week if it held steady, analysts said.
"There is going to be fundamental support for the market," Goss said.
However, Hammond cautioned that Wall Street's strength could run out of steam and that a correction could have serious implications for the local market.
"Wall Street is starting to defy gravity. If it reverses...we could follow it down to a large extent," Hammond said.

The market faces a rash of economic indicators to guide it next week. The much-delayed trade figures for October will be released on Monday, with analysts looking for a surplus of 900 million rand, up from 670 million in September.

On Thursday the current account details will be released in the Reserve Bank's Quarterly Bulletin and October PPI, also out on Thursday, is expected to move higher to a year-on-year 7.9 percent from 7.6 percent in September.
Reserves, due out on Friday, are seen up slightly, with analysts predicting the total end-month figure at 10.38 billion rand, marginally up from 10.28 billion in October.
Company results due next week include interim results from heavyweight industrial groups Richemont Ltd and Rembrandt Group Ltd on Monday, and Sappi Ltd year results on Tuesday.
